issue: stamphog_connected is a project-wide any-repo check, so the toggle can appear active for inbox PRs whose specific repo has no Stamphog config

verdicts.evidence: pr72680_tree/products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81 (get_stamphog_connected → has_reviewable_repo_config(team_id)); pr72680_tree/products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-126 (project-wide .exists() over any synced+enabled repo config); pr72680_tree/products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1141-1155 (per-repo gate in process_inbox_pr_review: logger.info + silent return when the PR's repo has no config)
verdicts.notes: The described behavior exists: stamphog_connected is a project-wide "at least one repo" signal while the actual inbox-review gate is per-repository and silently no-ops (logged only) for uncovered repos, so a multi-repo team with partial Stamphog coverage can see the toggle enabled yet get no reviews for PRs in unconnected repos. But it is low-stakes and largely by design: the help_text at settings.py:50-54 already states the "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository" semantics (the finding's fallback fix is effectively done), the settings endpoint has no repository in context so per-repo scoping is ill-defined for a project-wide per-user toggle, and the failure mode is fail-closed (skipped review, no wrong output). Valid observation, UX-copy-level at most — not must/should fix.

verdicts.evidence: has_reviewable_repo_config (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125) indeed has no repository filter (project-level any-repo check), and queue_inbox_pr_review (:126-141) documents the per-PR repo-config resolution as a "silent no-op without one" — the finding's mechanics are accurate. But the serializer copy is not overstated: stamphog_review_inbox_prs help_text (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py, diff hunk) uses necessary-condition phrasing ("Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository"), and stamphog_connected help_text says "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository" — exactly the project-level semantics implemented. Neither promises every inbox PR gets reviewed.
verdicts.notes: The finding self-identifies as "not a hard bug" (behavior matches the PR's stated design) and requests only a help_text wording tweak with no code-path change. The per-repo downstream gating is intentional and documented in the facade docstring. At most this is optional copy polish; there is no correctness, contract, security, or reliability damage, so it falls below the keep bar.

verdicts.evidence: settings.py:73-82 get_stamphog_connected → has_reviewable_repo_config(team_id), which is team-level "any synced+enabled repo exists" (facade/api.py:112-125). The review itself is gated per-repo: tasks.py:1140-1153 filters StamphogRepoConfig on repository__iexact=<PR repo> and returns silently (info log stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable) when absent. Frontend (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1061-1069) gates toggle interactivity only on stamphog_connected. So connected-repo-A + Inbox-PR-in-repo-B → enabled toggle, silent no-op. Mismatch is factually real.
verdicts.notes: Real coarseness mismatch, but low stakes: the silent no-op is intentional, documented fail-closed design (facade docstring api.py:141 "silent no-op without one"; task docstring tasks.py:1123-1124 "self-scoping"), and a review on an unconnected repo is impossible regardless (no App installation). The primary suggested fix (repo-aware signal in the settings serializer) is infeasible — no PR repo is knowable at settings-serialization time; the toggle is inherently project-level. Worst case is UX confusion (no verdict, no explanation) in the edge case where connected repos and Inbox PR target repos diverge. The help_text already documents the team-level condition, though not the finer per-repo gate. Valid observation worth a UI-copy/observability tweak at most, not a defect requiring a fix in this PR.

this_experiment_findings.title: UI gate is team-wide while the actual review gate is per-repository, enabling a switch that silently no-ops
this_experiment_findings.problem: stamphog_connected reports whether the team has at least one synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig for any repository (has_reviewable_repo_config checks .exists()). The actual review only runs when a config covers the PR's own repository (gated inside process_inbox_pr_review, silent no-op otherwise). A team with Stamphog connected for repo X whose self-driving work lands PRs against repo Y sees the 'Let Stamphog review your Inbox PRs' switch enabled, turns it on, and every subsequent review is silently dropped — no error, no feedback, and the toggle looks healthy. The model docstring itself states the toggle 'only takes effect for teams with a synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig covering the PR's repository', which the UI flag does not check.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: At minimum, scope the frontend hint to the mismatch: when connected but the Inbox PRs' repositories are not covered, the switch description should say reviews only run for repositories synced to Stamphog. A fuller fix is to compute stamphog_connected per repository the team's self-driving tasks actually target (the tasks product knows the team's repositories) and reflect that, so the switch state matches what will really happen.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Same claim: stamphog_connected is a team-wide any-repo .exists() while the review gate is per-repository, so the switch can be enabled and silently no-op for PRs in uncovered repos.

fresh_votes.evidence: The facts in the finding are accurate. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns `.exists()` over the team's synced, enabled configs for any repository. products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81 exposes that value as `stamphog_connected`. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1133-1147 then filters on `repository__iexact=repository` and returns quietly, logging `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable`, when no config covers the PR's repository. products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066 uses `stamphog_connected` only to disable a switch that is still off.
fresh_votes.refutation: This is how the code is meant to work, and it is documented; it is not a defect. The switch is a per-user preference for future Inbox PRs. When the user flips it, those PRs don't exist yet, so there is no repository to check. A per-repository check cannot be done at that point. The flag's own help_text (settings.py:50-54) says it means "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". It only decides whether the switch has anything to act on at all. The `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` help_text (settings.py:27-33) says the review "only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository". The task docstring (tasks.py:1122-1123) calls the per-repository skip an intentional, self-scoping no-op. The skip is logged, so it is observable. For repositories that are covered, the switch does what it says. The suggested fix is to guess which repositories self-driving tasks will target, which is a product and UX improvement rather than a correctness bug. The earlier validator on this finding also marked it is_valid=false.

fresh_votes.evidence:
The code does what the finding describes. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns `.exists()` over the whole team. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1135-1149 filters on `repository__iexact=repository` and returns quietly, logging `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable`, when no config covers the PR's repo. But the team-wide check is on purpose and documented, not a hidden mismatch:
- products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:50-53: the help text defines stamphog_connected as "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". Its only job is to disable the switch when Stamphog is not set up at all.
- products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27-32: the toggle help text says it "only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository".
- products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75 (`test_stamphog_connected_requires_a_synced_enabled_repo_config`) pins that team-level contract.
- products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:137-141 and tasks.py:1123-1124 describe the per-repo no-op as by design: it scopes itself to repos where the Stamphog App is installed.
- products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1062-1068: the UI uses the flag only as a "not set up yet" gate.
fresh_votes.refutation:
The toggle is a per-user preference that covers all future Inbox PRs. It works correctly for every repo connected to Stamphog. Stamphog can't review a repo where its GitHub App isn't installed, and that follows from the product setup, not from a bug in this code. The flag's contract (at least one connected repo, used only to disable the switch when nothing is set up) is stated in the serializer help text and locked in by test_settings_api.py:60-75.

A per-repo check would not fit a settings switch anyway. The switch applies to PRs that don't exist yet, whose repos can't be known ahead of time, and the "silent" skip is an intended info log. At most this is a wording tweak to the switch description, which is a UX preference and not a defect. Nothing is lost that the user could reasonably have expected: a repo that isn't connected was never going to be reviewed.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Reachability: the trigger can happen in production. products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config` returns true when the team has any synced, enabled config (`.exists()`, no repository filter). products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:73-82 exposes that as `stamphog_connected`. products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1133-1146 filters by `repository__iexact=repository` and returns with only `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable")` when no config matches. So a team with Stamphog on repo X and Inbox PRs on repo Y can turn the switch on and get no Stamphog review for Y. That part of the finding matches the code.

Why this is not a defect: the coarse, team-wide check is a documented design choice, not an accident. settings.py:50-54 says in its help_text that `stamphog_connected` means "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository". settings.py:28-32 says the toggle "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository". tasks.py:1122-1123 describes the per-repository no-op as intentional self-scoping. The flag only decides whether to disable the switch when nothing is connected at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1068). It never promises that every repository is covered.

The switch is opt-in and changes nothing else. Nothing is lost or wrongly approved. Stamphog just does not run on repositories where its GitHub App is not set up, which is how per-repository GitHub App installs normally work, and the user connected those repositories themselves. At most the switch description (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1054-1057) could mention that it only covers repositories connected to Stamphog. That is a copy/UX preference, and the suggested fix of computing coverage per target repository is speculative scope creep. The original validator also marked this finding invalid.
fresh_votes.refutation: The mismatch can happen, but the code and its docs mean it on purpose. `stamphog_connected` is documented as "at least one synced, enabled repository" (settings.py:50-54). Per-repository self-scoping is the documented behavior of process_inbox_pr_review (tasks.py:1122-1123, 1144-1146). The flag's only job is to disable the switch when Stamphog is not set up at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1063-1068). An opt-in switch that has no effect on repositories the user never connected to Stamphog is expected GitHub App scoping, not a correctness defect. What remains is a copy tweak, which is a style/UX preference.

this_experiment_findings.title: stamphog_connected is team-wide while the toggle takes effect per-repository, so "connected" does not mean reviews will run
this_experiment_findings.problem: get_stamphog_connected returns true when the team has at least one synced, enabled StamphogRepoConfig for any repository, but the actual gate (per the model docstring and _start_stamphog_review) is a config covering the specific PR's repository, checked inside the queued task with a silent no-op. A user who connects repository A and turns the toggle on gets a connected-looking UI while inbox PRs against repository B are silently never reviewed. The UI copy in CodeReviewScene.tsx ("Connect a repository to Stamphog first. Stamphog is not set up for this project yet.") reinforces the reading that one connection is sufficient.
this_experiment_findings.suggestion: At minimum, keep the help_text and UI copy explicit that connection is per-repository and uncovered PRs are skipped silently. A stronger fix is to make the flag answer the question the toggle actually needs (for example, accept the team's connected repositories from the Inbox context), or surface the silent no-op as a log/audit event so a user can diagnose why a PR was not reviewed.
this_experiment_findings.match_reason: Identical claim: stamphog_connected is a team-wide any-repo exists() while the actual gate is per-PR-repository, so the toggle looks connected for PRs against an unconfigured repo.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Premise confirmed by tracing the flag from producer to consumer in /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215:

1. Flag is team-wide, no repository parameter: products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125 `has_reviewable_repo_config(team_id)` is `.for_team(team_id).filter(enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False).exclude(installation_id="").exists()`. products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:72-81 returns it as `stamphog_connected`.

2. Actual gate is per PR repository, silent on miss: products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1137-1152 resolves `StamphogRepoConfig ... .filter(provider="github", repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True, ...)` and on `None` does `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable", ...)` and `return`. No run row, no PR comment, nothing reaches the UI.

3. The trigger is the product's own default, not an edge case: products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:302-316 binds EVERY repo in the installation with `defaults={"team_id": ..., "enabled": False}` and the comment says "connect them but don't start reviewing until a human toggles each on". So a team that enabled repo A and left repo B at its synced-but-disabled default has `stamphog_connected=True`, the toggle on, and inbox PRs against B skipped silently.

4. Copy reads as project-level: settings.py:27-33 toggle help_text "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository (see stamphog_connected)"; products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1054-1057 row description is unconditional ("When a self-driving implementation from your Inbox opens a pull request, Stamphog reviews it and approves it if it passes"); the disabledReason at 1066-1067 says "Connect a repository to Stamphog first". Only the model docstring (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:277-280, "covering the PR's repository") states the per-repo rule, and users never see it. `stamphog_connected` is the sole conditional input to that row (grep: line 1066 is its only use in the scene).

5. Tests only cover the team-level semantics: products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75 parameterizes on one repo config; nothing exercises the enabled-A/disabled-B case.
fresh_votes.refutation:
Attempted refutations:
(a) The `stamphog_connected` help_text (settings.py:50-54) is accurate for what it computes and only makes a claim about the false case ("has nothing to act on"), so the field itself is not wrong. This holds, but it does not cover the toggle's help_text or the UI row description, which are what a user reads and which imply one connected repo is enough.
(b) The flag's only consumer is a disabledReason gate for the "nothing connected at all" state, where it is correct. True, but the finding is about the copy that surrounds the toggle in the connected state, not about the disabled gate.
(c) The skip is logged server-side (tasks.py:1152). It is info-level and internal; no user-facing signal exists, so this only helps an operator, not the user the copy misleads.
(d) Overlap with GB16, which also names the per-repo gap as a secondary point. Overlap does not make it false; both resolve with the same one-sentence copy change.
None of these defeat the core claim. The stronger suggestion in the finding (make the flag per-repository aware from Inbox context) is not warranted, because the settings endpoint has no PR/repo context; the minimal fix is one sentence in the toggle help_text and the UI description saying reviews run only on repositories enabled in Stamphog. Real but minor, so consider.

fresh_votes.evidence: Premise verified in the worktree. `has_reviewable_repo_config` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:112-125) is a team-wide `.exists()` over `StamphogRepoConfig` with no repository argument. The real gate in `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1140-1152) filters `repository__iexact=<PR repo>` and returns after only `logger.info("stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable", ...)` when no config covers that repo; the webhook re-review leg does the same per-repo resolve (tasks.py:179-186). The model docstring already states the per-repo rule (products/review_hog/backend/models.py:279-280 "covering the PR's repository"), but the toggle's help_text says "Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository" (products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:30-32) and the `stamphog_connected` help_text describes "at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository" (settings.py:50-54); the UI disabled message (products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067) reads at project level. Tests confirm the per-repo silent no-op is the intended design, not a bug: `test_inbox_receiver_leg_noops_without_a_reviewable_config` has an explicit `different_repo` case (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:947-971, comment "Self-scoping (decision): toggle on without a synced+enabled config covering the PR's repository is a silent no-op"). `test_stamphog_connected_requires_a_synced_enabled_repo_config` (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_settings_api.py:60-75) only exercises team-wide semantics. No test, guard, or copy closes the gap between "project has a repository connected" (what the flag and copy say) and "this PR's repository is connected" (what the gate needs). Reachable trigger: a team with repo A synced and Inbox tasks producing PRs against repo B sees the toggle on and enabled, and reviews never run, with no user-visible signal.
fresh_votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The `stamphog_connected` help_text is literally accurate ("at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository") and never promises reviews for every PR, so the flag itself is not wrong. (2) The disabled-state UI message only fires when nothing is connected at all (CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066), which is correct for that state. (3) The silent no-op is a recorded design decision with a dedicated `different_repo` test (test_tasks.py:953, 958-971), and the skip is logged server-side with team and repository, so it is not a behavioral defect. These narrow the finding: the stronger suggestions (per-repo flag from Inbox context, audit event) are out of scope and the diagnostic already exists. What survives is only the toggle help_text at settings.py:30-32 ("when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository"), which contradicts the model docstring's "covering the PR's repository" and can mislead multi-repo teams. That is a real but minor copy-precision issue, not a bug, hence consider rather than should_fix. It also overlaps GB16's second point.

fresh_votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production, and it is the default state after connecting, not an edge case:

1. Sync binds every user-accessible repo in the installation but seeds them disabled: `products/stamphog/backend/presentation/views.py:309-316` (`defaults={"team_id": ..., "enabled": False}`, comment: "an installation can surface hundreds of repos, so connect them but don't start reviewing until a human toggles each on"). Webhook-added repos are also created `enabled=False` (`products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:632-636, 665-674`). So a team's normal shape is N synced configs, a subset enabled.

2. `has_reviewable_repo_config` (`products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:113-125`) is a team-wide `.exists()` over `enabled=True, connected_by_user_id__isnull=False, installation_id != ""`, no repository argument. One enabled repo flips `stamphog_connected` to true for the whole project.

3. The real gate is per-PR-repository: `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1138-1152` filters `repository__iexact=repository, enabled=True` and on no match logs `stamphog_inbox_pr_repo_not_reviewable` at info level and returns. No run row, no PR comment, no UI signal.

4. Inbox PRs do target multiple repos per team: signals picks the repository per report from a repo-selection artefact (`products/signals/backend/auto_start.py:624-628`) and `SignalsTeamConfig.autostart_base_branches` is a dict keyed by repository (`products/signals/backend/models.py:139`, used at `auto_start.py:518-519`). So "repo A enabled, PR against synced-but-disabled repo B" is an ordinary multi-repo team.

5. Copy: serializer help_text `products/review_hog/backend/api/settings.py:27-33` ("Only takes effect when the project has a synced, enabled Stamphog repository") and `settings.py:50-54` ("at least one synced, enabled Stamphog repository") describe a project-level condition; UI `products/review_hog/frontend/CodeReviewScene.tsx:1066-1067` says "Connect a repository to Stamphog first", which reads as one connection being sufficient. The model docstring (`products/review_hog/backend/models.py:277-280`) is the only place that says "covering the PR's repository".

Net: the flag/copy imply project-level sufficiency while the effect is per-repository; in the common partially-enabled state a user sees a healthy toggle and gets no review for PRs against a disabled repo.
fresh_votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) The `stamphog_connected` help_text is literally accurate ("at least one synced, enabled repository") and the flag's stated job is only to decide whether the toggle can act at all, so the serializer field itself is not wrong; the mismatch is confined to the toggle help_text and the UI string. (b) Per-repo enablement is a deliberate, product-wide stamphog invariant (webhook reviews also skip disabled repos), and the Stamphog settings expose a per-repo enable list, so a user who enabled only repo A has already made that choice in the product. (c) The skip is not fully silent server-side: `tasks.py:1152` logs team and repository, so operators can diagnose it. (d) Making the flag per-repository would require the settings endpoint to know the Inbox's future target repos, which it cannot; the "stronger fix" in the suggestion is not warranted. None of these make the user-facing copy accurate, so the finding survives as a copy-precision issue only. Severity stays at consider: no incorrect behavior, no data risk, fix is one sentence in help_text and one in the UI string.
